headline: SILVER CRATERS 5% IN ONE SESSION TO $73.78 — HAWKISH FED FEARS SLAM PRECIOUS METALS
snippet: Silver plunged 5.00% on May 19 to $73.78/oz as Middle East conflict fears and hotter-than-expected US inflation data strengthened expectations for central bank rate hikes. The move reverses recent gains and leaves silver down 7.43% over the past month, despite still sitting 123% above year-ago levels — the sixth consecutive year of structural deficits provides a floor, but rate-hike fears are in the driver's seat.

headline: Gold Slips to $4,542 — Tests 8-Week Low as Rate-Hike Speculation Mounts
snippet: Gold fell to $4,542/oz on May 18, its lowest level since late March, as hotter-than-expected inflation data led investors to price out Fed rate cuts and spark talk of a possible hike before year-end. A stronger US dollar and rising Treasury yields added pressure; gold is still 41% above year-ago levels but down 5.78% over the past month.

headline: SGML TANKS 15%: Sigma Lithium Fights Brazil Court Ruling, Calls It Coordinated 'Fake News' Attack
snippet: Sigma Lithium (TSXV: SGML) shares fell 15% on May 18 after a local Brazilian judge issued a ruling tied to waste disposal allegations at the Grota do Cirilo lithium operation, requiring a potential US$10M collateral. The company filed an immediate appeal, denied wrongdoing, and said the ruling coincides with a coordinated misinformation campaign — this despite reporting record Q1 earnings just days earlier.

headline: COPPER US PREMIUM EXPLODES on Tariff Bets as Comex Hits Record; ING Forecasts 600kt Deficit
snippet: US copper prices hit a record on the Comex as traders front-run anticipated tariffs on refined metal imports, widening the premium over London prices. ING Group forecasts a 600kt refined copper deficit in 2026, while China's April refined output fell 3% and Gulf shipping disruptions are squeezing sulfur supply — a critical input for copper smelting.

headline: Rare Earths Americas Surges 26% on NYSE Debut, Raises $63M to Chase US Heavy Rare Earth Discovery
snippet: Rare Earths Americas (NYSE American: REA) raised $63.3M at a $368M valuation on its NYSE debut, with shares opening 26% above the $19 IPO price. The company is targeting a US-based heavy rare earth discovery at a moment when Washington is aggressively pursuing rare earth supply independence from China.

headline: China Finds New Rare Earth Deposits in Frozen Northeast — Cheaper Extraction Could Cement Dominance
snippet: Chinese scientists identified a new type of rare earth formation in Heilongjiang and Jilin provinces — loose sand and gravel deposits shaped by freeze-thaw cycles, unlike the clay-heavy southern deposits that dominate current output. The geology could enable more efficient, lower-cost, and less environmentally damaging extraction, potentially deepening China's already dominant position in global rare earth supply.

headline: SILVER INSTITUTE: 46M Oz Deficit Marks Sixth Consecutive Year of Structural Undersupply
snippet: The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projects a sixth straight annual deficit of approximately 46 million ounces, with cumulative draws since 2021 nearing 762 million ounces. China's silver imports topped 790 tonnes in early 2026 — driven by solar panel manufacturing — while COMEX registered inventories have fallen from 531M oz last October to roughly 315M oz today.

headline: Energy Storage Set to Claim 31% of Lithium Demand in 2026 — Recovery Signal for Beaten-Down Metal
snippet: A boom in battery energy storage is reshaping lithium consumption, with Guotai Junan projecting storage's share rising from 23% in 2025 to 31% in 2026 — eating into EV battery dominance. The shift is stoking cautious optimism for an accelerated price recovery in a lithium market battered by years of oversupply.

headline: Uranium Spot Tops $100/lb as AI Datacenter Buildout Rewrites Long-Term Demand Forecasts
snippet: Uranium spot prices re-entered triple-digit territory as the rapid expansion of AI data centres reshapes long-term electricity demand and reinforces the investment case for nuclear power. More than 85% of surveyed investors expect higher uranium prices through 2026, with Kazatomprom supply constraints adding structural pressure and utility under-contracting creating a long re-procurement runway.

headline: TOP ANALYSTS: Gold Miners Poised to OUTPERFORM Bullion in 2026 as Valuations Lag $4,500 Gold
snippet: A growing chorus of analysts argues gold mining equities are substantially undervalued against a metal that's rallied 40%+ year-over-year, creating conditions for meaningful sector outperformance. Operational improvements, rising free cash flow margins, M&A optionality, and sector undervaluation are cited as the structural drivers — the question is whether miners can hold costs as the gold price gives back ground.

headline: Mining M&A Hits $21.6B in Q1 2026 as Supply Chain Security Replaces Growth as Deal Driver
snippet: Global mining M&A recorded 121 transactions worth $21.6B in Q1 2026, extending momentum from 2025's 13-year-high of $93.7B. Supply chain security rather than pure growth has emerged as the defining deal rationale, with critical mineral assets and government-financing-eligible projects commanding the most attention from strategic buyers.

headline: NdPr Oxide Down 21% in April to $99.61/kg — Still 88% Above January Open Ahead of China Quota Decision
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide posted its sharpest monthly drop since Q1's rally began, falling 21% in April to $99.61/kg, though it remains well above the cost base of western producers including MP Materials and Lynas. The next key catalyst is China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement — expected in June — which will signal whether supply tightens or eases in H2.
